title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1RC1LB_1LD1RA_1LE0LB_---1LF_0LF0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1RC1LB_1LD1RA_1LE0LB_---1LF_0LF0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, but it is reduced to the left end. Lean proves from a closed tape language (windows of 4 cells) that any halt from blank tape happens with blank tape to the left of the head. By hand and in simulation, the only way there is F reaching the leftmost written cell, which it has never done in 1010 steps (it came to the second cell 4 times and read a 1 each time).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Every halt is at the left edge
claims.text: In the run from blank tape, any configuration where the machine halts is in state E reading a 0 with only blank cells to the left of the head. Proved from a closed tape language with windows of 4 cells (472 abstract configurations), whose only halting configurations have a left state that accepts the blank stream alone; halt_left_of is the left-hand mirror of TM.CTL.halt_tail_blank, proved in this folder.

claims.title: Shift rules, for every length
claims.text: Going right: C turns (100)^n into (111)^n, A turns (001)^n into (111)^n and passes over (1101)^n unchanged; each for every n and every tape around.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,093 cells have been visited and 29,159 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.026). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.516).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>10</sup> steps; the left end
claims.text: c/leftedge.c: 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt; 16 new leftmost cells (at steps 5, 12, 49, …, 664,325,733, 5,128,930,040; width 88,956 at the last); the leftmost cell held 1 every time the head was to its right; F stood on the second cell 4 times (reading a 1) and never on the leftmost.

claims.title: Only F on the leftmost cell can halt (by hand)
claims.text: An argument by hand, not checked by machine: A is entered only by moving right, so it never stands on the leftmost cell; the 0-writers that do (D on a 1, F) step off it at once, so the leftmost cell holds 1 while the head is to its right. With the Lean result, a halt needs E on a 0 beyond that cell; the one way there is F reading the leftmost 1 (F1 = 0LC), after which C, D and E step onto blank cells and E halts. F on the second cell reading a 0 leads to the same.

claims.title: Layers that grow about 2.8 times per epoch
claims.text: At the left-end records, with t = 1110 and u = 111100, the tape is a short left prefix and then layers of periodic words, the outer one with period u t^15 u t and an inner one with period u t u t^2 u u t^4. Their repeat counts at the records from step 225,725 on: 2, 5, 15, 40, 114 and 6, 19, 56, 159, 446; width 597, 1533, 4173, 11509, 31981 (ratio about 2.76); the time between records grows about 7.7 times.

claims.title: Does it halt?
claims.text: Not known. What is left is whether the few cells at the left end ever let F reach the leftmost cell (or the second cell on a 0).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 37,093 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Layers of 1110 and 111100
html: The head reaches a new cell at the left end only rarely (16 times in 1010 steps, each about 7.7 times later than the one before). At those moments, writing t = 1110, u = 111100 and tk as the number k, the tape is:

Each epoch the sweeps of the head between the ends rewrite the layers, and the repeat counts grow about 2.8 times (2, 5, 15, 40, 114 for the outer layer). The tape width grows the same way: 597, 1533, 4173, 11509, 31981.

sections.heading: A few cells that count epochs
html: The left 6 to 8 cells change only when the head comes back to the left end, and they run through a short cycle of patterns built from pairs 11 and 01 (110101, 110111, 111101, 111111, then a longer prefix), much like a small binary counter. The leftmost written cell always holds a 1 while the head is to its right.

sections.heading: Only at the left edge
html: The only halt is E reading a 0. Lean proves, from a closed tape language with windows of 4 cells, that any halt from blank tape has nothing but blank cells to the left of the head. By hand: the way to get there is F stepping onto the leftmost cell and reading its 1; then F writes 0 and goes left as C, C writes 1 and goes left as D, D writes 1 and goes left as E, and E halts on a blank cell.
F has come to the second cell 4 times in 1010 steps and to the leftmost cell never. Whether the left-end counter can ever let it is the open question.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.026). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.516).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,093 cells (14 left of the start, 29,941 right), with a density of 1s of 0.786.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A layered bouncer: sweeps across the tape lay down periodic layers of the words 1110 and 111100 whose repeat counts grow about 2.8 times per epoch, while a few cells at the left end count epochs; Lean proves that any halt is at the left edge, and the run halts only if F ever reaches the leftmost cell.
family: Bouncer with growing periodic layers (left-edge halt)
